newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Frisco sees '97 San Felipe gold output up.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Frisco sees '97 San Felipe gold output up.

text.p: Mexican gold miner Empresas Frisco SA de CV expects gold production from its San Felipe mine to be 90,000 ounces in 1997, a director said Monday.

Jesus Gutierrez Bastida told the Mexico Mining 1997 conference here that output would creep back up because of anticipated higher grades than those seen in 1996 which saw production dip to 72,000 ounces.
Gutierrez said output in 1995, the start-up year for the mine in the northern state of Baja California which is 100 percent owned by Frisco and and covers 400,000 hectares, was 92,000 ounces.
Frisco estimates that reserves of the mine are around 14 million mineral tonnes, of which Gutierrez said 2.5 million were proven at 1.2 grammes per tonne.
Given the size of the mine and the outlook, he said Frisco was hoping to move to more cost effective open pit mining there soon, switching from the underground techniques currently in operation.
"If everything proves OK we will mine by open pit methods soon," Gutierrez said, not specifying any date.
Gutierrez said intitial exploration at the mine took 2.5 years and found mineral reserves of 1.8 million tonnes with 4.6 grammes of gold per tonne and 30 grams of silver per tonne.
Frisco decided to invest $27 million in the San Felipe mine, building a 2,100 tonne per day crushing mill which has since been upgraded to a capacity of 3,000 tonnes.
Recovery rates, he said, have been 86-90 percent for gold and 60-70 percent for silver. He said current processing costs were running at $8.15 per tonne.

Gutierrez said objectives for 1997, where seven targets were being drilled and 20 areas of interest pinpointed, were to reduce cyanide, lime, water and floculant consumption and increase gold recovery.
Frisco was currently stockpiling two grades, hge said, one of between 1.7-2.0 grammes/tonnes and a second lower grade of 1.4/1.7 grammes/tonne.
